assumptions: A photon of definite frequency, or an energy increment of one radiation mode; this is not a claim that an arbitrary multimode state has a single frequency.
variables: E: energy quantum; h: Planck constant; nu: cyclic frequency; hbar=h/(2 pi); omega=2 pi nu.
formulaPatches.units: SI: E in joules, h and hbar in joule seconds, nu in hertz, omega in radians per second.
formulaPatches.regime: Radiation energy quantum; zero-point energy is not included.

sourceLocations.locator: Lecture 2, printed/PDF p. 3, photoelectric-effect discussion: E=h nu and h=2 pi hbar; omega=2 pi nu is the stated frequency-convention conversion.

assumptions: Free photon in vacuum; lambda is vacuum wavelength and p is momentum magnitude.
variables: p: nonnegative photon momentum magnitude; lambda: wavelength; k=2 pi/lambda: wave-number magnitude.
formulaPatches.units: SI: p in kg m/s, lambda in m, k in inverse m.
formulaPatches.regime: Do not apply without qualification to canonical versus kinetic momentum of light inside a material.

sourceLocations.locator: Lecture 2, printed/PDF p. 3, final full paragraph: p=h/lambda from E=cp and lambda nu=c; hbar k uses k=2 pi/lambda.

assumptions: Free-particle momentum eigenmode; a narrow momentum wave packet has only an approximate representative wavelength. The inspected derivation is nonrelativistic.
variables: lambda: wavelength; p: magnitude of momentum; h: Planck constant.
formulaPatches.units: SI: wavelength in m and momentum in kg m/s.
formulaPatches.regime: The wavelength uses momentum magnitude, lambda=h/|p_vector|. A localized wave packet has a wavelength distribution; zero momentum is the infinite-wavelength limit. The relation also has a relativistic extension, not audited here.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.1, printed p. 21 (PDF p. 24), Eqs. (2.7)–(2.8) and following unnumbered wavelength relation; p in this record is the momentum magnitude.

assumptions: Closed nonrelativistic quantum system with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian on the relevant state domain.
variables: Psi(r,t): position-space state amplitude; H: Hamiltonian; t: time; hbar: reduced Planck constant.
formulaPatches.units: H has energy units; both sides have energy times wavefunction units. In 3D single-particle normalization, Psi has units m^(-3/2).
formulaPatches.regime: First-order time evolution; for spin or many particles the state and coordinates must be extended. Not a general relativistic field equation.

assumptions: Time-independent self-adjoint Hamiltonian; an ordinary normalizable eigenstate psi_n belongs to D(H). Generalized continuum eigenfunctions instead require a distributional interpretation.
variables: psi_n: energy eigenstate; E_n: corresponding energy eigenvalue; H: Hamiltonian.
formulaPatches.units: H and E_n have energy units.
formulaPatches.regime: Spectral eigenvalue problem; continuum eigenstates may require generalized normalization, and the displayed discrete subscript does not imply every spectrum is discrete.

sourceLocations.locator: Chapter 2 opening, Eq. (2.3), printed p. 19 (PDF p. 22); stationary-state discussion on p. 20 and free-particle continuum on pp. 20–21.

assumptions: Normalized pure state in a position representation; any internal components must be summed in the norm.
variables: P(r,t): probability density, not probability at one exact point; Psi: wavefunction.
formulaPatches.units: For 3D position, P has inverse-volume units and Psi has inverse-square-root-volume units.
formulaPatches.regime: Probability for a region is the integral of P over that region.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 1.1, unnumbered Born probability-density equation, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 7); following paragraph distinguishes density from probability in a volume.

formulaPatches.theoryRelationship: Modern equation checked against authoritative lecture notes; retained historical references are provenance, not a claim that their original equations were inspected.

assumptions: Normalized pure state and orthogonal projector P_a=P_a dagger=P_a squared for the measurement event.
variables: psi: unit state vector; P_a: projector onto the event subspace; p(a): outcome probability.
formulaPatches.units: p(a) and the projector are dimensionless.
formulaPatches.regime: Projective measurement, including degenerate eigenspaces; a general measurement uses positive POVM effects rather than necessarily projectors.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.1, Eqs. (2.5)–(2.6), printed/PDF p. 3: orthogonal spectral projector and event probability; normalized state is Eq. (2.1) on p. 2.

formulaPatches.theoryRelationship: Modern equation checked against authoritative lecture notes; retained historical references are provenance, not a claim that their original equations were inspected.

assumptions: rho is a positive trace-class operator with trace one; each E_a is a bounded positive effect with 0<=E_a<=I, and the effects sum to identity (discrete outcomes).
variables: rho: density operator; E_a: POVM effect; p(a): event probability.
formulaPatches.regime: Pure or mixed states and discrete generalized measurements; continuous outcomes require a POVM measure. Effects specify probabilities but do not uniquely specify the post-measurement state.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 3.1.2, Eqs. (3.19)–(3.21), printed/PDF p. 6, and positivity/completeness explanation on p. 7; source F_a is this record's E_a.

formulaPatches.theoryRelationship: Modern equation checked against authoritative lecture notes; retained historical references are provenance, not a claim that their original equations were inspected.

assumptions: For the displayed equality chain, psi is normalized and rho=|psi><psi|. For an arbitrary mixed rho, use only <A>=Tr(rho A), not a single-ket expectation.
A is self-adjoint and the expectation exists; for an unbounded A, use states in the required operator/form domain and a finite absolute first moment.
variables: A: observable; rho: density operator; psi: state; angle brackets: ensemble expectation.
formulaPatches.units: The expectation has the same units as A.
formulaPatches.regime: The trace expression applies to normalized pure or mixed density operators. The single-ket equality is the pure-state specialization; an ensemble average need not be an observed eigenvalue in an individual trial.

formulaPatches.units: Psi has units length^(-3/2); the integral is dimensionless.
formulaPatches.regime: Not ordinary normalization of ideal position or momentum eigenkets, which use delta-function normalization.

assumptions: Cartesian position and canonical momentum on a common suitable dense domain, for example Schwartz functions on R; the identity operator on the right-hand side is implicit.
variables: x: one coordinate operator; p: its canonical momentum; i: imaginary unit; hbar: reduced Planck constant.
formulaPatches.regime: For multiple Cartesian coordinates, [x_i,p_j]=i hbar delta_ij; this is not the algebra of arbitrary angular or compact coordinates.

assumptions: AB and BA must both be defined on the chosen common domain; no commutativity, boundedness or self-adjointness is implied by this definition.
formulaPatches.units: Commutator units are the product of the units of A and B.
formulaPatches.regime: Algebraic definition, not an independent dynamical law.

assumptions: A normalized state with canonical x and p, finite variances and sufficient common-domain regularity; this is a sufficient domain restriction for the displayed operator derivation.
variables: Delta x and Delta p: standard deviations in the same quantum state, not instrumental errors.
formulaPatches.regime: State-preparation variance bound; it is not a general measurement-disturbance relation.

assumptions: Closed-system evolution generated by a self-adjoint time-independent Hamiltonian for the displayed exponential.
variables: U(t,t0): unitary propagator; H: Hamiltonian; t0: initial time; psi: state vector.
formulaPatches.regime: For time-independent self-adjoint H, the unitary exponential acts on the Hilbert space; the strong Schrodinger derivative requires an initial state in D(H). A time-dependent H generally requires a time-ordered propagator under suitable existence assumptions.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.1, Eq. (2.10) and following unnumbered exponential, printed/PDF p. 4; source sets initial time to zero and uses hbar=1; self-adjoint generator on p. 3.

formulaPatches.theoryRelationship: Modern equation checked against authoritative lecture notes; retained historical references are provenance, not a claim that their original equations were inspected.

assumptions: Closed-system unitary evolution (or the full system plus environment), with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian and a positive trace-one density operator.

The differential equation requires differentiability and a defined commutator; finite dimension suffices. For unbounded H, require the relevant products and derivative on a suitable domain rather than assuming every trace-class rho is differentiable.
variables: rho: density operator; H: Hamiltonian; [H,rho]: commutator.
formulaPatches.units: Both sides have energy units because rho is dimensionless.
formulaPatches.regime: Not a generic reduced open-system equation: tracing out an environment may introduce dissipative and memory terms.
